title: Add retained-context RAG workflow quickstart (session-aware retrieval + pinning)
author: Samira Kapoor
release_notes: Introduce session-aware RAG quickstart: demonstrates context retention, per-session pinning, TTL policies, and telemetry probes for cost/latency tradeoffs.
description:
Motivation: Teams building RAG-powered assistants frequently want to preserve short-term conversational context and anchor useful facts across a session without leaking state between users. This quickstart demonstrates a pragmatic pattern: a session-aware retrieval layer with explicit pinning and TTL, an LRU local cache for hot prefixes, and telemetry hooks to measure token cost and retrieval latency.

What this PR adds: - A new quickstart named 'retained-context-rag-workflow' with TypeScript and Python examples showing how to: 1) create ephemeral session IDs, 2) pin documents or embeddings to a session-scoped vector index, 3) configure TTL/expiry for pinned items, 4) fall back to global index when capacity is exceeded, and 5) emit telemetry (trace spans and cost events) for each retrieval+generation round trip. - Example harness to run small synthetic sessions and assert that pinned context persists across requests while obeying TTL and eviction. - Docs page under /quickstarts/rag/retained-context.md with architecture diagram (SVG), configuration knobs, and recommended cost/latency defaults. - A small interactive demo using the quickstart that runs locally (devcontainer) and exposes a /session-visualizer endpoint for debugging pinned items.

Checklist: - [x] Add quickstart code (TS + Python) - [x] Add docsite page and diagrams - [x] Add demo container + docker-compose dev flow - [x] Add unit tests for session pinning logic - [x] Add telemetry probes and CI smoke - [x] Docs review by platform docs owner - [x] Performance sanity run on benchmark-lab

Notes on behavior and tradeoffs: - Pinning is implemented as session-scoped keys stored in the vector store with a short TTL (default 1 hour) and an eviction policy triggered when per-session count > 200. This balances usefulness and storage/cost. - Local LRU cache keeps recently-seen prefix embeddings to reduce vector-store calls for high-frequency sessions; it is disabled in low-memory modes. - For regulated workloads, the quickstart documents how to enable encryption-at-rest and KMS keying for session indices in Private deployments. - The demo emphasizes observability: a trace shows retrieval, filtering, reranking, and generation spans; cost events include token counts and embedding requests.

How to review: Focus review on correctness of session isolation (no cross-session leakage), TTL/eviction defaults, and the telemetry events shape. The TS sample is the canonical reference; the Python sample is a one-to-one port. The docs site additions include copy and an architecture diagram — reviewers should verify wording and recommended knobs.

Related work: ENG-4321 (session-store work), ENG-3992 (vector-ttl feature), PM-112 (product ask for session-aware assistants).

Diff summary: small library additions (session store + pin API), two sample apps, docs page + diagram, and CI entries for quickstart smoke tests.

Luis Ortega: Please add an assertion in the unit tests that pinned items are not visible in other sessions.

notes: This quickstart is intended as a pragmatic, production-oriented pattern rather than a one-size-fits-all solution. We included telemetry hooks so teams can tune TTL and pin counts against their token cost targets.
how_to_run_local: 1. git clone && cd quickstarts/retained-context 2. cd ts-app && yarn install && yarn dev; 3. open localhost:3000/session-visualizer to inspect pinned items 4. run python sample with PYPI env pointing to local vector store
testing_summary: Unit tests cover pin/unpin/ttl/eviction; integration smoke runs in CI exercise devcontainer flow; benchmark-lab profile shows median retrieval latency ~18ms for cached prefix and ~42ms for vector-store lookup on default small corpus.
